summary: Include both verses used in the cistern quotation

rationale: Both source goals are place names; I.6 requires an opponent.

summary: The LB 106 lowering predicates contain ko- and belong in ko-Preterit.
rationale: Both ko-manḥáttal-li and ko-mánḥatte are overtly marked; the introductory ḥəlli does not determine their box.

summary: Merge the ko-Preterit quotation into its existing ko-Preterit occurrence
rationale: The target form is ko-naḥət, not the unprefixed Preterit Intransitive naḥət. The same 47/73 occurrence is already quoted more fully in nḥt-1.I.t.ko-preterit.1. Consolidate it there, retaining the additional grammar reference 640, rather than leaving the ko-form in the plain Preterit box or creating a duplicate.

summary: Assign the descent to Qamischli to sense 1, not sense 6
rationale: The Turoyo naḥitina l-i=Žazire l-i=Qaməšlu describes going down to named places. Both the entry and 31/2 translate zogen wir herunter. It illustrates sense 1 herab-/hinabsteigen; sense 6 losgehen auf describes an attack, which is absent here.

summary: File ko-manḥáttal-li / ko-mánḥatte under ko-Preterit
before: naqla ḥəlli…naḥiti, ko-manḥáttal-li gweto, ko-mánḥatte aʕmayye əšmo d-zaytune w ṭlamṯo d-laḥmo
after: naqla ḥəlli…naḥiti, ko-manḥáttal-li gweto, ko-mánḥatte aʕmayye əšmo d-zaytune w ṭlamṯo d-laḥmo
rationale: The stem-III verbs illustrated are explicitly ko-prefixed Preterit forms ko-manḥáttal-li and ko-mánḥatte. Plain Preterit examples in this stem have manḥat- without ko-. The glossary distinguishes ko-Preterit as a separate box, including within stem I of this entry. A ko-Preterit box is needed in stem III for this quotation.

summary: Routine counts are compressed evidence only, not additional decision records: 395 I.1 Preterit Intransitive, 117 I.1 Infectum, 98 III.1 Preterit. Counts do not validate individual analyses or reset cell quotas.
The I.6 hostile target is distinct from a geographic l- goal. Correct 31/2; PrS 7/15 also belongs to geographic motion. The ʕal- attacks in PrS 15 supply an alternate target marker.
The I.5 Infectum input contains three actual examples (MM 97, LB 83, 36/6), not four including a placeholder. ??? is an uncertainty note attached to 36/6. No deletion is warranted.
I Preterit-wa is securely established by naḥətwo in JTM 1.5/1. The reduced hair form nəḥtiwa and the deictic waste-extent naḥitowa remain unresolved; translation alone cannot settle their paradigms.

III Infectum-wa is secure in full-n repeated procedural lowering (JL 14.9/3, 17.5/9). JL 13.12/12 additionally changes to apparent 1sg gmanḥatwayno, flattened to German wir; withhold it pending confirmation.
Nonvolitional I descent is not automatically Detransitive. The unloading tənḥito is an Infinitiv even where German uses an event framed as abgeladen waren.
Inherited notes and existing wording are retained. Corrections list canonical example IDs; existing counts in entry.md explicitly describe the input before those corrections.
Batch 2 continues batch 1 cumulatively: no prior accepted sense, example, idiom or correction is removed. I.1b social decline is additional, not a renumbering of I.8 or I.9.
104/19 overt object -la belongs to the established chess sense I.3; its positive/negative contrast shows no need for another chess sense.

Talay 1/106 is the LB 106 passage already quoted in the entry: retain batch 1 movement of nḥt-1.III.t.preterit.3 to ko-Preterit. Talay 1/77 likewise supplies the existing LB 77 reflexive command, while its reflexive Preterit fills a genuinely empty cell.

Round 2 only. Jan English is project machine translation, retained verbatim in selected excerpts; semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo. Round-1 proposals are retained as the baseline and are not repeated in this JSON.
Geographic migration in Jan 1.40/1766–1767 belongs to I.1, as already established by round 1's correction of 31/2. Do not widen the hostile-target I.6 or repeat that entry correction.

Round 1 already established I Preterit-wa and III Infectum-wa. Reader claims that these boxes are absent are stale; only thin cells are supplemented. Repeated predicates in one verse receive separate decisions, not repeated identical quotations.

Jan mixes recollected dialogue, technical prose and liturgical quotations. Publication vocabulary is supported by journal titles, issue numbers, serialisation and writing predicates in Turoyo. The crown clauses Jan 3.29/726–727 are quoted Syriac and are not selected as fresh Turoyo paradigm evidence.
Vapour, Holy Spirit, curse and words from mind to heart retain directed descent. The red layer on snow has an uncertain material/source and is not securely a precipitation example.
Only compact classifications, without verse text, were supplied for some routine tokens. Their decisions retain those classifications provisionally; no unprovided context is reconstructed.
Verify naḥənno contractions, PrS 65/5 Naḥitit and 67/16 Naḥən against the editions/audio; do not silently normalise them.
Resolve manaḥtile (JL 12.13/13), noḥətto yo (77/7), naḥitowa (JTM 5.2/86) and nəḥtiwa (MAC NE Samson the hero/12) before quoting uncertain paradigm assignments.
JL 9.9/9 has a German translation longer than the supplied verse. Is its alignment correct? It is not quoted here.
Confirm feminine moisture i daḥṯayo with printed noḥət (JTM 2.8/4) and the person contrast in JL 13.12/12 gmanḥatwayno versus German wir.
For MAC NE Dilo and Falako/53, does the challenge imply battlefield entry, ordinary descent or dismounting? No example is selected from this ambiguous passage.
Does the liturgical use denote taking a service turn conventionally, or physical movement down from a seat? The repeated named-office construction motivates provisional technical subsense 2b.
Is the apparently unrelated Tərto Zaré paragraph in the inherited III Imperativ ruḥux example note an accidental attachment? No text is removed without source verification.
Is first-person naḥətne in Talay 1/77 a dialectal vowel, an idiolectal form, or a transcription slip? Preserve it pending verification.
For 112/105, is descent to the world a conventional birth expression? A single instance with an explicitly elevated location does not yet justify a separate birth sense.

Is naḥətlonele in Jan 1.53/2596 a transitive I form or a contraction/transcription issue for III? Likewise naḥətwoli in Jan 3.2/32 lacks the full causative onset. Neither is published as a new I transitive paradigm.
Does Naḥət bu ṭanqiṣayḏe (Jan 2.31/5195) denote undertaking the reduction of the fast, acquiescing, or participation? The proposed b- construction is withheld pending clarification.
Are kmaḥto/maḥto in Jan 2.4/1139–1142 dialectal nḥt forms or another lemma? The source m is retained and their I allocation is withheld.
Resolve reduced Nəḥtiwo/naḥətiwo (Jan 1.34/1415; 1.50/2309) and unrealized naḥətowa (Jan 2.31/5177) between Preterit-wa and Infectum-wa; no silent vocalic normalization.
Is nəḥətto in Jan 4.I/125 a productive Part act. or a lexical low adjective? Is konoḥatle (Jan 3.56/1635) singular agreement with plural xabre or a different suffix analysis?
Does the red layer in Jan 1.27/1282 actually fall as atmospheric dust? Is Jan 3.21/474 plural naḥiti followed by singular naḥət a companion reference or a transcription issue?
Close the parenthesis in sense 4

summary: Correct the spelling of heruntergestiegen
rationale: The German past participle of heruntersteigen is heruntergestiegen; the current spelling omits e in -stiegen.

summary: Correct the third-person verb in the idiom translation
before: abases himself and come to me
after: abases himself and comes to me
rationale: The subject of the coordinated English verbs is He: he deigns, abases himself and comes. The source 42/14 also has the same third-person subject through kmanḥət nafše w gdoṯe l gabi. This corrects agreement without changing the chosen tense or wording.

summary: Downward orientation/extent also has timber, teeth, cloth, rocks and sinking body parts as subject; participant changes alone do not warrant senses.
Snow, alongside rain, is a precipitation subject; no separate snow sense.
The material-flow frame includes blood, pus, saliva, grape juice and loose grain as well as water, tears and earth.
Animate livestock, natural-force causers, body-part patients and full-n food-removal predicates preserve controlled lowering; general maḥt- placement remains under mḥt.
Later batch adds teeth reaching the chin, food entering the stomach, childbirth framed as downward emergence, and falling grave boards; these participant/path variants do not each establish a sense.
Market and shop relocation remains spatial descent, not a new commercial sense; successive feminine and masculine forms in 1.16/604 need agreement review.
Low regard for the language is related evaluative lowering, but nəḥətto may be a lexical adjective rather than a productive Part act.; no paradigm example selected.
Blessings descending from God extend the lowered theme; return aircraft passengers and bride dismounting retain controlled downward motion.
Modern military deployment, including the peace-force designation, retains dispatch to a combat area.
